1. The given graph shows that the variable taken
on Y axis remains constant with variation in
temperature.
As $V \propto T$, $\frac{V}{T}$ is constant at constant pressure.
Therefore, a graph of $\frac{V}{T}$ Vs. $T$ runs parallel to
the temperature axis.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

2. Since 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 $l$ volume
at STP, 2 moles of the same gas should occupy
44.8 $l$ volume at STP. Volume of a given mass of
a gas necessarily depends on the temperature
and pressure.

3. (i) 2 moles of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 4$ N oxygen atoms
(ii) 1 moles of $\mathrm{Fe}_2\mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow 3$ N oxygen atoms
(iii) 0.5 moles of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \rightarrow 2$ N oxygen atoms
(iv) 1 mole of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} \rightarrow 1$ N oxygen atoms
(v) 0.25 moles of $\mathrm{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 0.75$ N oxygen atoms.
$\therefore$ DEABC is the required order.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

4. A balloon filled with air and tightly tied, when
hung close to the source of heat, bursts after
some time as the pressure inside the balloon
increases with increase in temperature.
Hence, the correct option is (c).

5. The formula $\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{HPO}_4$ corresponds to $\mathrm{M}^{+1}$
and $\mathrm{HPO}_4^{-2}$ radicals. $\mathrm{M}^+$ ion can form $\mathrm{MClO}_4$,
$\mathrm{M}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ and MH with the radicals $\mathrm{ClO}^-$, $\mathrm{CO}_3^{-2}$,
and $\mathrm{H}^-$, respectively.

6. $V_1 = 6 l$
$V_2 = 8 l$
Let $P_1 = 100 \text{ mm of Hg}$
$P_2 =$?
$P_2 = \frac{P_1 V_1}{V_2} = \frac{100 \times 6}{8} = 75 \text{ mm of Hg}$
25% decrease in pressure is found.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

7. $PV = nRT \Rightarrow P = \frac{nRT}{V} = \frac{RT}{V}$ ($n =$ constant)

(a) $P = \frac{R \times 200}{200} = R$

(b) $P = \frac{R \times 300}{600} = \frac{R}{2}$

(c) $P = \frac{R \times 400}{200} = 2R$

(d) $P = \frac{R \times 500}{600} = \frac{5R}{6}$
The correct decreasing order of pressure
exerted by the gases are $2R > \frac{5R}{6} > R > \frac{R}{2}$.
Hence, the correct option is (b).

8. The formula of sodium bicarbonate is $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$.
Molecular mass = 84
% of sodium = $\frac{2300}{84} = 27.4\%$
% of hydrogen = $\frac{100}{84} = 1.2\%$
% of carbon = $\frac{1200}{84} = 14.3\%$
% of oxygen = $\frac{4800}{84} = 57.11\%$
P = carbon, Q = hydrogen, R = sodium, S =
oxygen
This can be done by comparing the molecular
composition.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

9. Vapour density of gas = $x$
Molecular mass of gas = $2x$
$2x$ g of gas contains $6 \times 10^{23}$ molecules.
$\frac{3x}{2}$ g of gas contains $6 \times 10^{23} \times \frac{3X}{2} \times \frac{1}{2X}$
$= 4.5 \times 10^{23}$ molecules
Hence, the correct option is (a).

10. Both glucose and acetic acid have the same
empirical formula, i.e., $\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{O}$. Neither ethyl
alcohol nor sucrose has an empirical formula.
The empirical formula of ethene is $\mathrm{CH}_2$ and
that of acetylene is CH.
